subject: Travel Media Briefing — Creator Contracts Digest: What to Watch in Your Press Trip Agreements
body:
Good morning,

This week's digest covers a topic many of you have asked about: navigating deliverable discrepancies between signed contracts and follow-up communications from destination partners.

Key takeaways:
• Signed agreements are the legal baseline — any additions or revisions communicated via email should be treated as informal amendments unless countersigned.
• Best practice: request a formal addendum or at minimum a written acknowledgment from both parties when scope changes post-signature.
• Deadline conflicts between contract and email: default to the more recent written communication from the brand side, but flag for explicit confirmation before departure.
• Stories and short-form video added post-contract are increasingly common — document them carefully as they affect your production schedule.

Full article at travelmediabriefing.example/creator-contracts-digest-april-2026

Until next week,
The Travel Media Briefing Team

TRAVEL MEDIA BRIEFING — April 14, 2026

IN THIS ISSUE:

1. FTC ENFORCEMENT UPDATE: Disclosure language in newsletter footers is now under active review. The 'clear and conspicuous' standard applies to email as well as social. Recommended language for hosted trips: disclose at the top of any sponsored section, not just in a footer.

2. PRESS TRIP CONTRACT RED FLAGS: Three clauses to watch in 2026 tourism board agreements — (a) non-disparagement clauses that restrict honest review, (b) approval rights over published content, (c) exclusivity windows that block competing destination coverage. If any of these appear, negotiate or decline.

3. CREATOR RATE BENCHMARKS Q2 2026: Newsletter dedicated features (300+ words) averaging $450–$800 for lists under 10K subscribers. Blog posts with SEO value averaging $600–$1,200 per placement depending on DA.
